title: Glasgow modifié Alcohol Withdrawal échelle (GMAWS)
formula:
| GMAWS Scoring Criteria | | | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Parameter | Score 0 | Score 1 | Score 2 |
| Tremor | None | Present with arms extended | Present with arms at rest |
| Sweating | None | Moist skin | Drenching sweat |
| Hallucinations | None | Uncertain, or patient reports but not distressed | Present and distressed |
| Orientation | Orientated | Uncertain or disoriented in one domain | Disoriented in ≥2 domains |
| Agitation | None | Anxious/restless | Distressed or pacing |

how_to_use.why:
- Fournit une alternative structurée et simple au [CIWA-Ar](nabda:calc.ciwa-ar-alcohol-withdrawal), qui repose sur des signes objectifs plutôt que sur des symptômes rapportés par le patient.
- Réduit la variabilité inter-évaluateurs.
- Aide à standardiser et à ajuster en toute sécurité le traitement par benzodiazépines, ce qui améliore les résultats du sevrage et réduit les risques de sous-sédation comme de sur-sédation.
how_to_use.when: Used to determine benzodiazepine dosing as well as timing of reassessment for patients who are at risk for alcohol withdrawal.
how_to_use.pearls:
- Validé en milieu hospitalier ainsi que pour les unités de sevrage médical.
- Non spécifiquement validé aux urgences.
- Non recommandé en usage ambulatoire.
- Ne capture pas les symptômes subjectifs (p. ex., nausées, céphalées), ce qui peut limiter la sensibilité en cas de sevrage précoce ou atypique.
- Peut être moins familier que [CIWA-Ar](nabda:calc.ciwa-ar-alcohol-withdrawal) dans certains établissements des États-Unis.

next_steps.advice:
- Utiliser le GMAWS pour guider la posologie des benzodiazépines et la réévaluation.
- Envisager d’utiliser le lorazépam au lieu du diazépam chez les patients présentant une insuffisance hépatique, un âge avancé ou un métabolisme altéré suspecté.
- Surveiller les signes de sursédation par benzodiazépines, en particulier chez les patients ayant des comorbidités.
- Intensifier la prise en charge si les symptômes s’aggravent ou deviennent réfractaires au traitement malgré des administrations répétées.
next_steps.critical_actions:
Initiate urgent evaluation and consider ICU transfer or escalation of care if any of the following occur:

- GMAWS ≥8 for more than 1 hour.
- Heart rate >140 or <50 bpm.
- Systolic blood pressure >180 mm Hg or <90 mm Hg.
- Seizures.
- Respiratory rate ≤12/min or signs of hypoventilation.
- Decreased level of consciousness or airway compromise.
- Urine output <0.5 mL/kg/hr.
- Significant comorbid CNS, cardiac, or respiratory conditions.
- Inadequate response to repeated benzodiazepine doses.
next_steps.management:
Les auteurs du GMAWS recommandent le traitement suivant basé sur les symptômes. Cependant, le jugement clinique doit être utilisé pour évaluer l’ensemble du tableau clinique avant d’administrer des médicaments.

| Score GMAWS | Médicament recommandé | Intervalle de réévaluation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | Aucune benzodiazépine | Réévaluer dans 2 heures |
| 1–3 | Diazépam 10 mg PO/IV ×1 Alt : Lorazépam 2 mg | Réévaluer dans 2 heures |
| 4–8 | Diazépam 20 mg PO/IV ×1 Alt : Lorazépam 4 mg | Réévaluer dans 1 heure |
| 9–10 | Diazépam 20 mg PO/IV ×1 Alt : Lorazépam 4 mg | Réévaluer dans 1 heure |

evidence:
The GMAWS was first published in 2012 by[McPherson et al.](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22328545/)and is the combination of two other previously published alcohol withdrawal syndrome tools. The goal of it’s development was to bring standardized assessment of alcohol withdrawal symptoms to the area of study. When compared to the CIWA-Ar tool, this initial research showed patients monitored with GMAWS were found to have received fewer benzodiazepines in the first 24 hours, have more scores recorded on time, and a higher proportion of staff found it to be an easier assessment to administer. Despite the limited geographic region of study, lack of clinical endpoints identified, and allocation only by clinical site rather than randomly, the GMAWS showed good internal consistency and warranted additional study.

A more recently published 2024 retrospective cohort study by[Schonewald et al.](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38871256/)evaluated another adult population who were admitted to general medicine or surgery floors and carried a diagnosis of alcohol withdrawal. It also found a reduction in the median benzodiazepine dose administered, along with a significant reduction in the rate of delirium tremens.

While [CIWA-Ar](nabda:calc.ciwa-ar-alcohol-withdrawal) remains the most common tool for assessing alcohol withdrawal severity, GMAWS offers a simpler, more objective alternative that is preferred by some clinical staff, particularly in settings where ease of use is paramount. The choice between these tools should be guided by the clinical context, available resources, and the specific needs of the patient population.

Interpretation:

| 1–3 | Diazepam 10 mg PO/IV ×1 Alt: Lorazepam 2 mg | Reassess in 2 hours |
| 4–8 | Diazepam 20 mg PO/IV ×1 Alt: Lorazepam 4 mg | Reassess in 1 hour |
| 9–10 | Diazepam 20 mg PO/IV ×1 Alt: Lorazepam 4 mg | Reassess in 1 hour |
